Slug 'suspicious-site-warnings' derives from the exact listing name 'Suspicious site warnings' in the milestone=152 features_by_type listing (category 'Enabled by default', re-fetched 2026-09-06); folder v152/ per listing position; H1 is the listing name verbatim; the identity link chromestatus.com/feature/5427561449521152 appears in the at-a-glance table, specifications, and see-also.

The feature has no web-exposed API (verified: no Blink runtime feature, no web-features entry, no MDN doc — all linked on-page), so the declared inventory is the observable behavior contract: verdict mapping, warning UI + choices, 30-day bypass allowlist, and the two admin policies ChromeStatus names as controls. All five items map to documented fragments across all nine dimensions; reference-contract.json claims implementation-sufficient. Held-back point: three contracts are intrinsically non-public or undocumented (server-side WARN signals, allowlist sync behavior, a suspicious-verdict-specific owner review path) — the page declares each as undocumented rather than omitting them, which is the honest ceiling for this feature.

Model-first structure: why the middle confidence tier exists (interstitial vs silence), then the no-API boundary up front (the question a developer asks first), then the verdict contract, UI choices, allowlist, site-owner paths, and policy controls in MDN article order. The 'suppression and failure modes' table gives the negative space (when a warning does NOT appear), which for a warning surface is the contract developers and admins actually need. Disambiguation note for the older SafeBrowsingSuspiciousSiteTriggerQuota feature prevents a likely codebase-search confusion.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation tables no horizontal overflow mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on the browser's layout engine: intrinsic sizing and logical properties before hardcoded dimensions; keep overflow contained rather than letting wide content stretch the page.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: every table sits in .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto}; wide comparison tables get a min-width + table-layout:fixed so they scroll inside the wrapper; overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1/lede and code cells for long tokens (feature names, policy names, URLs); pre{overflow-x:auto} so verbatim C++/JSON scrolls internally. Confirmed by reading the 360px screenshot.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use loading="lazy" on iframes well outside the initial viewport to avoid fetching competing resources; never lazy-load above-the-fold content.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: the showcase demo iframe is far below the fold (examples section, after nine content sections) and carries loading="lazy" with an explicit height (520) to avoid layout shift when it loads.
